definition: The harmless error rule states that if a mistake is made during the creation of a will, but it is not significant enough to affect the overall validity of the document, the will can still be recognized as valid and entered into probate court. This rule sometimes allows for minor mistakes in the signing and witnessing of the will, but errors in the writing requirement of the will are typically not considered harmless. It is important to note that not all states have accepted this doctrine.
